notes: Item 2, what I found about the daemons' lock read: it is neither retried nor merely moved after the pidfile - it is GONE for a daemon. use_run reads the lock only when --run is empty or the command is not a daemon (`[ -z "$run" ] || { [ "${1:-}" != any-run ] && [[ $CMD != _* ]]; }`, cluster.sh:622), and both daemons are started with --run, so cmd__heartbeat and cmd__sampler reach `printf '%s\n' "$$" >…pid` without a single lock read; the heartbeat's later reads are inside its loop, where a failed `kube patch` falls back to kube_lock_get and, when that fails too, logs and continues to the next cycle. The suite's own case says the same in its name. So the answer to the question as asked: there is no start-up lock read left to retry.

One behaviour worth the reviewer's eye, not a defect of this round: the guard fails OPEN on a failed lock read. lock_names_other_run (cluster.sh) returns 1 when kube_lock_get fails or the namespace has no lock, so copy_is_ours returns 0 and the caller acts, and kube_lock_get is a plain `kube get` with no retry of its own (unlike the kube_read execs). The source says this is deliberate - `A read that failed, and a namespace with no lock at all, say nothing: the caller then acts as it would have` - and failing closed would wedge a live run on a flaky API server. The window is narrow (another run must hold the lock and the read must fail at that moment), and I report it rather than file it.

Item 4, the guard list walked against the source: every kubectl exec that writes, kills or removes in the shared pods goes through runner_exec (:1471) or postgres_exec (:1149), with psql_write through postgres_exec, runner_put and scale_to; every other exec in the file is a read (psql_at, the df, the .rc and .log reads, cpuinfo, cpu.max, the copy-back's tar and gzip, replay-checksum, replay-verify-bundle) or one of the exemptions the header names and I confirmed: up's work around kube_lock_take, down's label-scoped delete, the heartbeat's JSON-patch test op, the sampler's and stop_daemon's own processes, nats_box's pod chosen by the run label, apply_manifest's three callers, and the replay's two long streams after stop_copy and after runner_exec's reset. My round-7 omission is closed: apply_manifest is now named in that list by its three callers.
